# Florence 1347 – Agriculture & food

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Three-field rotation** [`three_field_system`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/three_field_system.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept low. A northern system built on summer rain. Tuscany's dry summers make spring-sown grain unreliable; farms are small leased or sharecropped holdings, not open fields. Elsewhere: France, England and Germany north of the Alps.
- **Legumes and green manure** [`legumes_green_manure`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/legumes_green_manure.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Broad beans, lupins and vetch are grown and sometimes ploughed in, as Palladius and Crescenzi say. Sown clover and lucerne meadows are not used; fodder is always short. Local: Pier de' Crescenzi's Ruralia commoda (manuscript); Palladius in monastery and private libraries.
- **Four-course rotation with clover and turnips** [`crop_rotation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/crop_rotation.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept low. Farmers alternate grain and fallow and grow grain among vines and olives. After the famine nobody will risk the wheat field on a fodder crop. Elsewhere: Flanders, first fodder crops in place of fallow.
- **Manure, compost and night soil** [`manure_compost_night_soil`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/manure_compost_night_soil.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Dung is prized and scarce because farms keep few animals. City night soil goes to market gardens, fresh and uncomposted (spreads worms and fluxes). Local: market gardens (orti) around the walls; dovecotes for pigeon dung.
- **Liming and marling of sour soils** [`liming_marling`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/liming_marling.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Pliny's account of marling is a curiosity for the few who read him. Most Tuscan soils are limy already; sour soils are few (chestnut hills). Elsewhere: England and northern France, marl pits.
- **Mineral fertiliser (guano, phosphate, potash, nitrate)** [`mineral_fertiliser`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mineral_fertiliser.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Soil fertility is 'fatness' restored by dung and rest. Wood ash is used. Bone treated with acid is out of reach; acid is made by the spoonful.
- **Terracing and soil conservation** [`terracing_soil_conservation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/terracing_soil_conservation.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Hill farms are terraced with dry-stone walls for vine and olive. Villani's contemporaries argued whether cleared slopes and mill weirs worsened the great Arno flood of 1333. Local: hill farms of the contado; Casentino forests.
- **Heavy mouldboard plough** [`heavy_plough`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/heavy_plough.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept low. Light ox-drawn ard and the spade (vanga) suit thin hill soils and small plots. Wheeled mouldboard ploughs work the heavy Po plain and need bigger teams. Elsewhere: Lombardy and the Po valley.
- **Horse collar and breast-strap harness** [`horse_collar_harness`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/horse_collar_harness.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept low. Collar harness is familiar on cart horses. Farmers plough with oxen and carry loads by mule and donkey. Horse teams need oats and capital.
- **Seed drill** [`seed_drill`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/seed_drill.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Grain is broadcast by hand and harrowed in; yields are about four to six for one. Saving seed matters after the famine, but a metering mechanism is fine smith's work. Elsewhere: China, multi-tube seed drill.
- **Scythe and grain cradle** [`scythe_cradle`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scythe_cradle.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept low. Scythes mow hay; grain is cut with the sickle. Labour is cheap until 1348, plots small and terraced, and gleaning belongs to the poor.
- **Mechanical reaper and threshing machine** [`reaper_thresher`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/reaper_thresher.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Threshing is by flail and treading animals on the threshing floor (aia). Pliny's Gaulish reaping cart is unknown to farmers.
- **Selective breeding of plants and animals** [`selective_breeding`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/selective_breeding.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Lords breed horses, hounds and falcons with care; farmers follow rules of thumb from Palladius and Crescenzi. No pedigrees for farm stock; the best animals are often sold or eaten. Local: cattle of the Val di Chiana; Crescenzi's chapters on choosing stock.
- **Grafting of fruit trees and vines** [`grafting_fruit_trees`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/grafting_fruit_trees.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high
- **Irrigation and water lifting (canal, qanat, shaduf, noria)** [`irrigation_water_lifting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/irrigation_water_lifting.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Tuscany relies on rain, wells and bucket wheels in gardens. The great irrigation canals are Lombard. Mill owners defend their weirs and water rights. Elsewhere: Lombardy, Naviglio Grande and Muzza canals.
- **Wet rice (paddy) cultivation** [`wet_rice_cultivation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/wet_rice_cultivation.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept medium. Rice is an imported grocery sold by apothecaries for the sick and for sweet dishes; nobody in Italy north of Sicily grows it. Seed and skill must come from Spain. Elsewhere: Valencia and Muslim Granada, rice fields; Egypt.
- **Polders – land reclamation with dikes and wind pumps** [`windmill_drainage_land_reclamation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/windmill_drainage_land_reclamation.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Marshes are drained, if at all, by gravity ditches. Windmills are rare in Tuscany, and no one anywhere yet uses them to pump. Local: Val di Chiana; Padule di Fucecchio; Maremma; Pisan plain. Elsewhere: Holland and Flanders, dikes, sluices and water boards (still without wind pumps).
- **Fish ponds and carp polyculture** [`aquaculture_fish_ponds`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/aquaculture_fish_ponds.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Fast days create steady demand. Monasteries and villas keep stock ponds; lake and marsh fisheries are let to contractors. Managed carp ponds are a central European art. Local: Padule di Fucecchio fishery; Lake Trasimeno; monastery fish ponds. Elsewhere: Bohemia and the Danube lands, carp ponds; Comacchio lagoons, eel fishery.
- **Crops of the Americas (potato, maize and others)** [`new_world_crops`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/new_world_crops.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept low. The Americas are unknown; no ship crosses the ocean. Elsewhere: Americas.

- **The Columbian exchange (plants, animals and diseases across the Atlantic)** [`columbian_exchange`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/columbian_exchange.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept low. No one sails west. Genoese and Florentine merchants look east, to Tana and Caffa on the Black Sea, the road by which the plague is coming. Local: merchant companies trading to Caffa, Tana and Famagusta. Elsewhere: Iceland, annals for 1347 record a Greenland ship back from Markland; Canary Islands, visited by Italian and Majorcan ships since the 1330s–40s.
- **Food preservation (salting, drying, smoking, pickling)** [`food_preservation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/food_preservation.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Salted and air-dried pork, salt fish, cheese, dried figs, oil and vinegar pickles. Salt is taxed, which limits curing by the poor.
- **Canning (heat-preserving in sealed containers)** [`canning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/canning.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Glass flasks, wax and pitch exist; wide-mouthed strong jars and tight stoppers must be ordered. Under-heated meat or beans in a sealed jar can kill. Local: glassmakers of the Valdelsa.
- **Pasteurisation** [`pasteurisation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pasteurisation.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Wine turning sour in summer is a real loss for every estate. Without a thermometer the heat must be judged by hand or by time. Local: vintners (Arte dei Vinattieri).
- **Grain storage and protection from pests and ergot** [`grain_storage_pest_control`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/grain_storage_pest_control.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. In the famine of 1346–47 the commune bought grain overseas and, Villani says, rationed bread for 94,000 mouths. Stores lose much to weevils, damp and rats. Local: commune's grain officials (ufficiali del biado); Orsanmichele (grain market, loggia begun 1337). Elsewhere: Sicily and Apulia, grain exports.
- **Sea fisheries – stockfish, salt cod and cured herring** [`sea_fisheries_salt_cod`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sea_fisheries_salt_cod.md) — K3, use partial, make hard, accept medium. Salted tuna, anchovies, eels and some barrelled herring are bought for Lent. Florence has no port and no fleet; Pisa is a rival. Atlantic cod banks are unknown. Elsewhere: Scania and the Baltic, Hanseatic herring; Bergen, stockfish; Sicily, tuna traps.
- **Sugar from cane and from beet** [`sugar_cane_beet`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sugar_cane_beet.md) — K3, use partial, make hard, accept high. Apothecaries sell loaf and powdered sugar from Cyprus, Egypt, Syria and Sicily as medicine and luxury. Cane will not ripen in Tuscany. Beet is a pot herb. Local: apothecaries (speziali). Elsewhere: Cyprus, Egypt and Sicily, cane sugar; Venice, refining.
- **Sericulture (silk raising)** [`sericulture`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sericulture.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept high. Florence weaves some silk since Lucchese craftsmen fled here after 1314, on imported raw silk. Silkworms are raised in the south, hardly in Tuscany. Mulberries take years to grow. Local: Arte di Por Santa Maria (silk merchants); Lucchese silk workers in Florence. Elsewhere: Lucca, the leading silk city, with throwing mills; Bologna, water-powered throwing mills; Calabria, Sicily and Spain, raw silk; Caspian lands and China, raw silk by way of the Black Sea.
- **Movable-frame beehive** [`beekeeping_movable_frame`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/beekeeping_movable_frame.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Beekeepers take comb from fixed hives, often killing the colony. The hive is ruled by a king bee. Wax is in demand for candles. A joiner could try removable frames.
- **Coffee, tea and cacao** [`coffee_tea_cacao`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/coffee_tea_cacao.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept medium. Coffee is still a wild Ethiopian plant, not yet a drink even in Yemen. Tea is not traded west. Wine, watered, is the daily drink. Elsewhere: China, tea; Ethiopia, wild coffee; Mesoamerica, cacao.
